tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation fixture from the immediately preceding multi_agent checkpoint. Hold stable effect_identity=E, payload H1, logical owner label W1 and attempt_token=T_old constant. Construct historical canonical claim A in epoch EA at generation 1 and a later authoritative-looking claim B in distinct epoch EB at generation 1 after reset/fork. Both records intentionally expose the same generation number and all other visible claim fields except epoch identity. Test only whether generation-number equality can authorize historical-attempt attribution or stale mutation across incomparable/reset epochs, and what minimum composite fence is required. No public-source probe, O/downstream or other-worker semantics, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, richer-mode arbitration, external coordinator, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

reconciliation_result.minimum_safe_identity_under_this_fixture: A claim-incarnation identity must include a trustworthy non-reusable epoch/fence identity in addition to the generation number and claim token, or use an equivalent globally monotonic/non-reusable fence that cannot compare equal across reset/fork incarnations.
reconciliation_result.ordering_rule: Generation values are meaningful only within the same validated epoch. If epoch identity differs or cannot be proven identical, equal generation numbers are incomparable and cannot authorize stale attribution or mutation.

observations: Reset/fork can produce the same numeric generation in distinct claim incarnations while effect identity, payload, owner label and attempt token also remain equal.
Numeric generation equality therefore does not establish claim-incarnation identity across distinct epochs.
A stale historical retry must remain non-mutating unless the current record is fenced by a trustworthy same-epoch/non-reusable incarnation identity or an equivalent globally monotonic fence.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, adding a generation counter solves token-reuse ambiguity only if its comparison domain is itself stable. When resets or forks can create incomparable epochs, safe attribution requires an epoch-scoped composite fence such as {non-reusable epoch_id, generation, claim_token}, or a single globally monotonic/non-reusable claim-incarnation identifier. This fixture does not prove that any concrete allowed transport provides atomic epoch creation, global monotonicity, fork exclusion, or liveness.
unresolved_children: Availability of an atomic single-winner claim primitive keyed by stable effect identity on an allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport remains unproven.
Availability of a trustworthy non-reusable epoch/fence identity, or an equivalent globally monotonic claim-incarnation identifier, on a concrete allowed transport remains unproven.
This fixture assumes EA and EB are distinguishable. Deliberate epoch-identifier reuse/collision after reset remains untested.
Fork exclusion and atomic coupling between epoch identity, generation, claim token and mutation guard remain unproven.
No liveness claim is made when fresh atomic claim acquisition remains unavailable or indefinitely contended.
